free_tier.stated: Open-source and 100% self-hostable. Public instance at *.pipenet.dev if you don't want to self-host.

egress.terms: No allowance is published for the public instance.; ingress: http-only

interface_detail: Node client plus a REST status API at /api/status.
chaining: Only useful as an HTTP ingress for an MCP or webhook endpoint.
binding_note: The only published control is a socket cap per client, so concurrency fails long before any byte allowance would. The transport is also HTTP-only, so a UDP datagram has no path at all.

identity_cost.detail: No account is described: the public instance is a hostname you point a client at. The README shows no signup.

reliability_note: Public instance is a courtesy run by the maintainer with no stated capacity or SLA.
confidence_note: A measured run against the public instance would show whether it is still up and what it rate-limits; the UDP question is already answered by the maintainer.

evidence.proved: Server options include maxTcpSockets default 10 and tunnelPort; the API is an HTTP tunnel server, no UDP or raw port.
Launch post and maintainer reply that the implementation is HTTP-focused and UDP support is not planned.

notes: Launched 2026-01-19. A localtunnel rewrite with multiplexing over one port, built for an MCP inspector. It is a software project with a courtesy public instance, not a capacity provider.

extras.wg_detail: HTTP-focused by the maintainer's own answer: The current implementation is HTTP-focused as that was the primary use case.
extras.volume_stated: No allowance is published for the public instance.
extras.transit_note: The pipenet.dev instance relays HTTP requests to the local client.
